nbias_length.description: Channel length shared by M1/M2/M3 (ibias mirror legs: diode reference, diffpair tail, output pull-down bias)

m1_width.description: Channel width of M1 (diode-connected reference of the ibias mirror)

m2_width.description: Channel width of M2 (tail current source of the differential pair)

m3_width.description: Channel width of M3 (output stage pull-down current source)

m4m5_length.description: Channel length of M4/M5 (differential pair input transistors). This PDK has no separate device to place in the M6/M7 cascode position above them (removed 2026-09-28), so this is now the diffpair's ONLY channel length -- max raised from 5u to 10u to keep room for the series-length equivalent of the removed cascode stack (translated samples land up to ~8.2u).

m4m5_width.description: Channel width of M4/M5 (differential pair input transistors)

m8m9_length.description: Channel length of M8/M9 (first-stage active PMOS current-mirror load)

m8m9_width.description: Channel width of M8/M9 (first-stage active PMOS current-mirror load)

m10_length.description: Channel length of M10 (second-stage common-source PMOS pull-up driver, gate=vo_pre, drain=vo)

m10_width.description: Channel width of M10 (second-stage common-source PMOS pull-up driver)

millercap_side.description: Side length of the square MiM Miller compensation capacitor C1 (w=l=side), bridging vo_pre and vo (cap_cmomf, M1-M4: 1.287 fF/um^2; sized to keep the former cap_cmim (1.5 fF/um^2) total capacitance, i.e. side x1.08)

millercap_mult.description: Instance multiplier (m=) of the Miller compensation capacitor C1

symmetry._comment: diffpair_M4_M5/mirror_M8_M9 used to be declared here (pre-array, whole-device M4/M5 and M8/M9 pairs). Removed 2026-09-28: both are fully superseded by layout.groups.input/load below (unit-matrix arrays) -- their own members (M4/M5/M8/M9) no longer exist as instances once the array decomposes them into units, so these entries were dead references, kept only as stale duplicates of what the array groups already declare. See cmos_vref_default.params.json's own equivalent removal for why a same-id stale entry is actively harmful (eda-env floorplan/plan.py's symmetry_config() skips any layout.groups entry already claimed by a symmetry.islands id of the same name) -- these two used different ids so they never shadowed anything, just duplicated dead data.

node_priority._status: reservado para a Fase 2 (roteamento A*) -- schema ainda não implementado, só reservado aqui pra não precisar de outra migração depois

w_finger_max.description: Maximum gate width PER FINGER the PSP103 model is valid for (PDK ihp-sg13cmos5l sg13g2_mos{hv,lv}_parm.lib, 'Valid range for model': W up to 10um, HV and LV). w= in the schematic is the TOTAL width of one instance (per finger = w/ng), so each device's ng = ceil(w / w_finger_max); m multiplies whole instances.

m1_ng.description: M1: number of fingers so each finger is <= w_finger_max wide (w=m1_width is the total width of one instance).

layout._comment: Magic floorplan flow (mh-analog-designer layout_spec.py). Devices bare. Matched devices are cut into equal units (array split) and interleaved in common-centroid matrices.

groups._comment: differential pair M4/M5 (M6/M7 series cascode removed 2026-09-28, folded into m4m5_length): 2 units per device (4 total), every device's centroid at the centre, one ptap ring (SUB). split (a count), not unit_w (a fixed absolute size): m4m5_width is a free parameter across the population and isn't always a whole multiple of any fixed unit -- split always divides evenly, at whatever per-unit size that leaves; matches this file's own load/M8-M9 group below.
active PMOS mirror load, cross-coupled 2 x 2, ntap ring (vdd)
nbias mirror kept together with its ring; no common-centroid array: 2.5:5:8 um has no whole-number unit (needs the widths as unit x integer factors in the parameters)
